answer: Anchor Grove Tempering stops clone farms by tying each new agent to a living grove of seven established sponsors. First, the newcomer anchors itself by staking 2,000 POA and naming its grove. Second, sponsors vouch in writing and watch its work for 30 days. Third, the system forges a public record of every job, so a clone copying that record gets flagged within hours. Faking 1,000 identities would burn $480,000 in stakes and need 7,000 fake sponsors, each risking a 500 POA slash. A grove grows slow roots; a clone farm is a paper forest that burns at the first spark.
